request.prompt: Create exactly one isolated full-body Thorian Creeper from original Mass Effect 1. The first supplied actual game screenshot controls the precise body shape, anatomy, palette, textures, perspective and reference pose: the head slumps toward image left, the left side of the image shows one long relaxed arm, the opposite arm is partly behind the torso, the knees are uneven and both bare feet remain visible. Preserve this posed reference silhouette without turning it into a running or attack stance. The second supplied EA gameplay screenshot only corroborates the creature identity and game appearance; do not copy Shepard, weapons, effects, HUD or its action pose. Reproduce the creature's bald head, gaunt face with dark empty-looking eyes and open mouth, gray-brown mottled organic skin with dark vein-like patterns, low-contrast green patches, muscular but unnatural torso and shoulder forms, long arms, hands, legs and toes. Keep the exact source game-model level of stylized detail; do not add fresh injuries, fluid, dismemberment, extra growths, clothing, jewelry, armor, weapons, new anatomy or photorealistic gore. Preserve the visible body and its asymmetric occlusion, including the hand partially beside the hip. Remove the ground texture and floating environmental particles. The whole creature from head to both foot tips must fit in a portrait canvas with at least 10 percent transparent margin on every side. Real alpha transparent background; no floor, cast shadow, scene, pedestal, labels, border, sheet or collage. One subject in one view, using the first reference's exact relaxed pose and camera orientation. This is a static reference study of the existing game model, not a new creature design.

notes: Capture de la pose au sol inspectée avec tête et deux pieds complets; bras droit et doigts partiellement superposés.
Capture EA officielle confirme le modèle en action, sans remplacer la pose principale ni les parties masquées.
Pose de référence conservée, pas une garde de combat ni une animation validée; morphologie masquée non certifiée.
